old: Its name has barely changed in thousands of years, drifting quietly down from a single ancient root.
Germanic languages nearly all echo it: Dutch says 'bij,' Danish and Swedish say 'bi.'
German speakers call it 'Biene' — a cousin word for the same striped insect.
clues: This small flying insect has a name that has barely changed in thousands of years, tracing back to an ancient root that already meant exactly the same creature.
It lives in a hive, visits flowers for nectar and pollen, and makes honey, which sets it apart from its stinging cousin the wasp.
People who stay very productive are called busy as one, children compete in a spelling one, and its German cousin is Biene.
